messages.report.silent: the bot said nothing: a turn opened no message.

report.spoke.one: the bot spoke: {count} message, unaddressed by anyone.
report.spoke.other: the bot spoke: {count} messages, unaddressed by anyone.

messages.report.stage1:
stage one came from a model: the room was read through the server at {origin},
so the decision to act is the measured watch model's and not a placeholder.
The words said above are still a stub in src/main.ts — this run generated no text.
messages.report.stub:
nothing above came from a model: the decision to act and the words said are
stubs in src/main.ts. What this run shows is the kernel — delivery, the gate,
the turn — and what it cannot show is whether the design holds up.

messages.ui.settings.decides.description: Local · the model the app carries. It is asked one question — answer, or stay quiet — and answers with a probability; it never writes a word into a room.
messages.ui.settings.decides.nothing-to-configure: There is nothing to configure here: the judgement is one question asked of a decision model, and a hosted chat endpoint has no such call. That is why the two halves are two cards.
messages.ui.settings.decides.title: Decides whether to answer
messages.ui.settings.organizations.title: Organizations
messages.ui.settings.organizations.description: Each organization is its own world on this machine: its own person, its own bots, its own rooms, messages, pictures and roster, all in its own directory. Switching reads the other one; it moves and deletes nothing. A name here is a label for the list — it never becomes the name of the person inside.
messages.ui.settings.organizations.name-hint: a name — shown in this list and nowhere else
messages.ui.settings.organizations.made: made — open it when you want to work in it
messages.ui.settings.organizations.delete-questio: Delete “{name}” and its directory? Rooms, messages, pictures and its roster go with it.
messages.ui.settings.machine.title: Models on this machine
messages.ui.settings.models.description: Seek asks two models two different questions. One decides whether a message is worth answering, the other writes the answer. The first is the app's own and is not configurable; the second is yours. It is set once for this machine: every organization answers with the same one.
messages.ui.settings.models.writes-description: Remote · an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Save below and this half uses it from the next turn.
messages.ui.settings.models.key-hint-saved: saved · ends {tail} · {length} characters · type a new one to replace it
messages.ui.settings.models.key-note: Kept in {path} on this machine, readable only by you. It reaches this endpoint's requests and nothing else — the store stays local, and the judgement never leaves this machine at all.
messages.ui.settings.models.saved: saved — this half uses it from the next turn
messages.ui.settings.source.config: Right now this half is the endpoint already configured on this machine ({path}). Save below and this half becomes yours instead.
messages.ui.settings.source.environment: Right now this half is the endpoint you started Seek with, from the environment. What you save here will not be used until you start it without those variables.
messages.ui.settings.source.none: No endpoint is configured: this half is the model the app carries, which cannot write a turn that calls a tool.
messages.ui.settings.source.settings: This half is the endpoint saved below.
